author: Mark Atwood
text: API contract confidence: 25% chance of missed issue. Least confident flags: JMAP-ic0j.26 (default-impl philosophy — there is no workspace-AGENTS.md decision on whether silent-no-op-default is acceptable; the maintainer may have intended this; filing as a question rather than a defect), JMAP-ic0j.37 (typed-vs-ad-hoc errors — labeled opinion because the AGENTS.md doesn't pick a side; the right answer is a workspace policy decision, not a per-crate fix). More confident: JMAP-ic0j.25 (supports_type doc conflict, verified by reading both crates' rustdoc), JMAP-ic0j.28-30 (publication-surface design decisions visible directly in the diff), JMAP-ic0j.32 (seed_object stringly-typed key + unvalidated value — the type-name typo footgun is verifiable mechanically). Uncertainty driven by: did not run cargo doc to inspect rendered HTML, did not check whether the four property enums currently appear in any third-party consumer's import paths (no published 0.x yet, so this is hypothetical SemVer-lock risk rather than active breakage), did not cross-check the canonical mail-server's own ic0j-equivalent review history to see if findings 26 and 37 have been previously deliberated. Would raise confidence if: (a) ran cargo public-api to enumerate the actual exposed surface, (b) checked git log on jmap-mail-server backend.rs for similar refactor discussions, (c) compared all 7 server siblings (mail, chat, calendars, contacts, tasks, filenode, sharing) to identify which divergences are calendars-only vs. workspace-wide drift.
